Grok Hackathon Pavia · 4 Nov 2026 · Trova

Can Trova find things through the Pi camera?

We photographed four table scenes with the Raspberry Pi camera and asked Grok 4.7 to find objects by name, by use and in Italian. Grok picked the correct box 31 times out of 32. Detection found every object with no false boxes, but it merges objects that touch.

31/32requests where Grok chose the correct box or correctly said "not found"
0false boxes from the wall, floor, chair or wood grain
3boxes that hold two objects (touching or overlapping)
10.8 smedian Grok call through Cursor (36 calls, max 19.4 s)
How it works

Three steps from photo to answer

Photograph

The Pi takes a photo of the empty table first and locks exposure and white balance from it. Every scene is shot with the same settings.

Box every object

Plain OpenCV compares each scene with the empty table and draws a numbered box around anything new. No AI in this step, 23 ms per frame.

Grok picks a box

Grok sees the numbered photo and a request, then answers with a box number, "not found", or a question when the request fits more than one box.

The four scenes

What the camera saw and what Grok named

Magenta boxes are drawn by detection. The names under each photo come from Grok's inventory of that scene.

The one miss: in scene 02 Grok read the second plug as a "flat-prong USB charger", so it answered box 2 instead of asking which plug.

When a request is ambiguous

Grok asks instead of guessing

"Do you mean the black bottle, the black cap, or the black plug?"

scene 01 · "the black object"

"Which black object do you mean: the bottle, a plug adapter, the charger, or the cap?"

scene 02 · "the black object"

"Do you mean the black bottle or the black cap?"

scene 04 · "the black object", after the plug was removed

After each question we answered "number 1" once, the way Trova's follow-up works, and Grok then picked box 1 every time.

Takeaways

What holds up and what to fix

Holds up

  • Requests by name, by use ("something to drink from") and in Italian all land on the right box.
  • Grok says "not found" for missing objects, including the plug once it was taken away.
  • The empty-table photo cancels the whole background: wall, floor, chair leg and wood grain give zero false boxes at the default threshold.
  • The cap is one box now. In the phone-photo dry run, without an empty-table photo, it split into two.

To fix

  • Touching or overlapping objects become one box. Grok picks the right box, but its centre is between two objects, so a grasp would miss.
  • A camera looking straight down would remove the overlap case (scene 02). It would not split objects that really touch (scene 03).
  • Grok mislabelled the second plug as a USB charger, so it skipped the question it should have asked.
  • Detection tags the pink highlighter as "red". It is only a hint for Grok, but it is wrong.
Setup

How this was run

Camera
Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W with Camera Module v2 (Sony imx219, fixed focus)
Photo
1640 × 1232, full 4:3 view, rotated 180°
Locked settings
shutter 30 ms · gain 3.28 · white balance 1.29 / 1.97
Detection
Trova's own find_blobs, threshold 30, minimum area 0.08% of the frame
Model
grok-4.7-low-fast through the Cursor CLI, using Trova's own prompts
Runs
One run per request, 36 Grok calls in total
This is a test of recognition only; the robot arm was not used. The timings go through Cursor, not the xAI API, so the live app will be faster and these are not demo numbers.
